channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [7] Field angle-independent high magnetoresistance and field angle-dependent coercivity in Fe3GaTe2/Phosphorus all-van der Waals spin valves at room temperature
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Haixin Chang, Yong Jiang

Authors: Zhiyan Jia, Yuxin Tian, Kun Ye, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant van der Waals magnetic material with spin transport studies.

Tags: #magnetism #vanderWaals #transport

Abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 02 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75103-8 The authors found that a room temperature magnetoresistance of 103% is achieved in all-van-der-Waals spin valves using Fe3GaTe2 and black phosphorus, and that the MR ratio is independent of field direction due to domain-wall-motion-driven magnetization switching dynamics in Fe3GaTe2.
